source.version: arXiv v1 (arXiv:2601.17769v1 [cs.HC], 25 Jan 2026), full PDF on file; complete markdown including Appendices A-C read, with recorded numbers checked against PDF pp. 1, 4, 6-7, 11-13, 23 and 28-30
source.title_on_document: Reflexa: Uncovering How LLM-Supported Reflection Scaffolding Reshapes Creativity in Creative Coding

supplement.where: Appendices A-C at the end of this PDF (pp. 23-30)
supplement.holds: System prompts (A), questionnaires and interview guide (B.1-B.4), participant demographics (Table 5, p. 28), and comparison/trend tables (Tables 6-12, pp. 28-30): Table 6 on p. 28, Tables 7-10 on p. 29, and Figure 18 and Tables 11-12 on p. 30. Table 10 contains self- and expert-rated outcome comparisons; Tables 11-12 report separate within-system version trends.

paper_design_summary: The paper reports formative workshops involving eight artists, three product designers, and six creative coders, analyzed qualitatively to inform the system (pp. 4, 6-7, Sections 3.1.1, 3.2.3 and 3.3.1). In the comparative study, 18 artists each used Reflexa and a baseline assistant with the same GPT-4o model, editor, and preview for a 30-minute creative-coding session per system; order was counterbalanced but randomization is not stated (pp. 11-12, Sections 5.1-5.3.2). Participants and three experts rated the artifacts on 7-point scales, with scores averaged across four versions for paired system comparisons and separate within-system version trend analyses (p. 13, Sections 5.3.3-5.4; pp. 29-30, Tables 10-12).

studies.label: Counterbalanced within-subjects user study (Reflexa vs. baseline LLM assistant; randomized order not stated)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of use of the two systems (Reflexa first or baseline first); every participant used both. The paper says the order was counterbalanced and does not say it was randomized.
assignment.quote: The order of system use (i.e., which system was used first) was counterbalanced across participants to mitigate order effects.
assignment.prereg_locator: No preregistration reported in the full text or Appendices A-C (PDF pp. 1-30).

arms.name: Reflexa
arms.description: LLM creative-coding assistant with integrated reflection scaffolds: tiered reflective prompt modes (R1-R3), version-node visualization, version manipulation (merge, modify)

arms.name: Baseline
arms.description: Single-threaded LLM chat interface that generates code, with the same LLM, code editor, and preview as Reflexa but no reflection scaffolds

participants.who: Artists (digital media, XR, interactive, and generative AI artists, ages 19-31) with prior experience in Processing or p5.js and LLMs, recruited by purposive sampling through social media and generative art communities; paid $14 for about 120 minutes
participants.quote: We recruited 18 artists with prior experience in creative coding and LLMs (Appendix B.5, Table 5) via purposive sampling through social media (Xiaohongshu, Weibo) and generative art communities.
participants.locator: p. 11, Section 5.1; p. 13, Section 5.4 ("small sample size (N = 18)"); p. 28, Table 5 (P1-P18)

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4o in both systems; Reflexa additionally uses text-embedding-ada-002 through Microsoft Azure. The baseline embedding configuration is not stated (p. 11, Section 4.2.3; p. 12, Section 5.2.3).
ai_tool.how_used: Both arms generate p5.js code from prompts. Reflexa adds reflection scaffolds (reflective prompts, version graph, merge and modify of versions); the baseline is a plain chat interface. The contrast is one AI configuration against another (p. 11, Section 4.2.3; p. 12, Section 5.2.3).

task.description: Produce a working interactive visual sketch in p5.js with an open thematic prompt, at least one interactive element, and at least two adjustable parameters; four sketch versions per system
task.duration: Two 30-minute creative-coding sessions, one per system (p. 12, Section 5.3.2)

outcomes.name: Expert-rated originality of the creative-coding outputs
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Three expert evaluators independently rated the creative-coding artifacts on a 7-point scale (p. 13, Section 5.3.3). Self- and expert-rated scores were averaged across four successive versions (p. 13, Section 5.4). Table 10 reports the overall paired system comparison; it gives no test-specific n or degrees of freedom, and the aggregation across expert raters is not fully specified. Supplementary version-wise results (p. 30, Table 12, Originality row): Reflexa mean v1 to v4 = 3.31 to 4.11 (Friedman p = 0.035, Page p < .001); Baseline mean v1 to v4 = 3.22 to 4.15 (Friedman p = 0.003, Page p < .001). These are separate tests of the version sequence within each system, not tests of a between-system difference or a difference in trends.

participants.who: Six creative coders recruited through creative-coding communities and university design programs, with 2-5 years of creative-coding experience and prior LLM-assisted coding experience. Backgrounds included creative media art, digital media art, and generative art. Participation was voluntary and uncompensated; employment/student composition is not stated.
participants.quote: We recruited six creative coders (4 male, 2 female, aged 22–28) with 2–5 years of creative coding experience across diverse backgrounds:

ai_tool.how_used: Participants reviewed Figma prototypes and a researcher-led creative-coding scenario; the text does not establish live use of a particular model in these workshops (p. 7, Section 3.3.1).

task.description: Review mid- and high-fidelity Reflexa prototypes, walk through a creative-coding scenario, and discuss reflective needs and design refinements. Think-aloud recordings were thematically analyzed; no scored creative-output comparison is reported (p. 7, Section 3.3.1).
task.duration: Two workshops, three participants each, 60-80 minutes (p. 7, Section 3.3.1).

eligibility.reason: The comparative study analyzed 18 people in both AI configurations, below 50 (p. 11, Section 5.1; p. 13, Section 5.4). System order was counterbalanced, but randomized order is not stated, so this is coded other rather than an RCT (p. 12, Sections 5.2.4 and 5.3.2). Expert ratings of the artifacts meet the output-scoring criterion; artifact self-assessments do not independently meet it (p. 13, Sections 5.3.3-5.4; p. 29, Table 10). The formative workshops report samples of eight, three, and six people, without a scored AI-treatment comparison (pp. 4, 6-7, Sections 3.1.1, 3.2.3 and 3.3.1); these counts are not added to the comparative sample. No randomized AI-assistance study is documented in this version. Context_class remains none because the unstated order-allocation method does not establish a definitively non-random observational comparison.

one_line_finding: With 18 artists in a within-subjects design, expert raters scored Reflexa sketches higher than baseline sketches on originality (3.67 vs 3.27, t = 5.51, p < .001), novelty (3.67 vs 3.33, t = 3.39, p = 0.001), and aesthetics (4.10 vs 3.60, t = 4.59, p < .001) (p. 29, Table 10).
notes: Read the entire 154078-character markdown, including references and Appendices A-C; checked the source PDF and Table 10 column alignment. S1 remains the comparative study; S2-S4 identify the separately reported formative datasets. Formative counts are recruitment/workshop counts, with no separate analyzed counts reported, so their n_analyzed values remain null and are not summed with S1. Participant overlap among these stages is not stated. The main study has 18 people; neither repeated versions nor expert ratings are additional participants. For Table 10, statistics_available lists test_statistic: means and SDs are printed, but test-specific n and degrees of freedom are absent, so arm_means_sds_ns is not claimed. Complexity and Evolution retain construct=other because the paper provides no scoring rubric mapping them more specifically. Version-wise analyses are supplementary within-system analyses; no expert Evolution between-system estimate is inferred. The self-report questionnaires on reflection, creativity support, interaction experience, and agency are not scored creative-output outcomes and are not added as such. No reported creative-output outcome was omitted under the form limit.
